title: Anamorphic
description: Anamorphic cinematography squeezes one image dimension during capture, usually horizontally by 2x, then expands it for presentation. Depending on the lens, that cylindrical squeeze can produce oval bokeh, directional flares, and distinctive edge behavior; a wide aspect ratio alone is not anamorphic photography.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The frame can hold a face and a landscape in the same breath because the desqueezed field is wide while the taking lens may still be a moderate focal length. Highlights streak sideways.
Out-of-focus lamps become ovals. The optic announces a movie without needing black bars glued onto a spherical image.
39:1. Cropping a Spherical 50mm and adding letterbox is an aspect ratio, not this glass.
It is also the wrong tool if you need clinical edges and round bokeh. Not every anamorphic lens flares the same way; do not treat Anamorphic Flare as automatic.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the frame should announce itself as widescreen glass: a night interior with oval lamps, a face in a wide city. Do not use it as a synonym for letterbox, and do not sprinkle blue streaks on every spherical shot.

blocks.text: Spherical has round bokeh and rectilinear edges with no squeeze. Anamorphic Flare is one artifact some anamorphic lenses produce, not the whole system.
Vintage Cine Glass can be spherical or anamorphic; vintage is coatings and contrast, not the squeeze. Black bars on a 16:9 file are not this technique.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Blade Runner uses anamorphic night interiors and city imagery as a widescreen optical fact. Inception's live-action photography is largely anamorphic widescreen.
La La Land and The Batman lean on oval highlights and directional flares as part of that glass. Borrow the squeeze behavior, not a copyrighted still.

blocks.text: Name the squeeze and the artifacts you actually want. Anamorphic 2x on [Subject], oval bokeh, horizontal flares, widescreen squeeze character.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Spherical footage with black bars, or a flare overlay without oval highlights. The tell is round lamps, no squeeze character, and a 16:9 image with mats.
Fix: oval bokeh, horizontal highlight streaks, desqueezed widescreen geometry. A wide aspect ratio alone is not anamorphic.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is anamorphic in film?
It is a lens system that squeezes one dimension at capture and expands it for viewing. Many such lenses add oval bokeh and directional flares. Widescreen shape by itself is not anamorphic.
Anamorphic vs Spherical

Spherical lenses do not squeeze; bokeh is typically round and edges stay rectilinear. Anamorphic lenses squeeze, then desqueeze, and often ovalize highlights. Letterboxing a spherical image does not convert it.
When should I use anamorphic?
Use it when you want the specific optical behavior of squeeze glass: oval lamps, horizontal flares, a wide field from a moderate taking length. Skip it if you only wanted black bars.
How do I prompt anamorphic for AI image or video?
Write: Anamorphic 2x on [Subject], oval bokeh, horizontal flares, widescreen squeeze character. Demand desqueezed geometry. Forbid round bokeh and simple letterbox.
